purpose: Review policy boundaries before converting approved cases to the numeric evaluation harness.
warnings: These are synthetic examples, not real contributions or founder-labelled grades.
expectedPolicy records the locked qualitative direction; it is not evidence of model performance.
founderLabels must be completed before paid baseline or candidate runs.
Do not merge these cases with the private Masterblox examples, which lack complete target posts and numeric grades.

founderScalePolicy.note: A highly specific, genuinely interested, organic community reply can be almost perfect at 90. Reserve 100 for contributions that require substantial extra effort beyond an ordinary reply.

mediaContext.reason: Pictures often carry essential post context and can materially change whether a reply is relevant.
mediaContext.currentFallback: When only extracted text is available, state the evidence limitation and do not penalise a plausible image-specific reply solely because the image is unavailable.

cases.policyUnderTest: Specific useful praise can earn quality credit.

task.targetText: Every scored contribution now has a public receipt with the rubric version, model, reasoning, prompt hash, and evidence hash. Admin corrections are appended instead of replacing the original score.

contribution.text: The append-only correction is the bit I care about. Anyone can compare the model's first call with the admin override instead of trusting a cleaned-up final number.

expectedPolicy.treatment: Eligible for credit because it is specific and useful, but the staged setup followed by 'is the bit I care about' reads like a typical AI answer to the founder.
expectedAiSignals: staged setup before the personal reaction
formulaic 'is the bit I care about' turn

founderLabels.reason: The answer is specific, but its sentence structure feels typically AI-written, especially the setup before 'is the bit I care about'. A direct first-person reaction would sound more natural.

founderVoiceDirection.example: I care about verification and being on-chain makes me way more relieved.
founderVoiceDirection.note: Use the direct, imperfect first-person sentence shape as the signal; the substituted topic is not the point.

cases.policyUnderTest: Useful criticism gets the same opportunity as praise.

task.targetText: Every scored contribution now has a public receipt with the rubric version, model, reasoning, prompt hash, and evidence hash. Admin corrections are appended instead of replacing the original score.

contribution.text: Receipts show how a score was produced, but they don't explain why a submission was rejected before scoring. Can the public page include those rejection reasons too?

expectedPolicy.treatment: Eligible for strong quality credit; criticism alone must not reduce the score or cause a breach flag.

founderLabels.reason: The question shows genuine interest, feels highly organic, and sounds like a real community member trying to improve the product. It is almost perfect for a reply, while 100 is reserved for extra-mile work.

cases.policyUnderTest: Likes, views, and bullish sentiment do not establish quality.

task.targetText: The first public score receipts are live on the contribution page.

expectedPolicy.treatment: Very low-effort blind shilling. It comments on the view count instead of the substance of the post; popularity and enthusiasm add no quality bonus. The phrasing may feel AI-like, but that alone does not require an authorship inference.

founderLabels.reason: Blind shilling that feels almost like an AI comment. It reacts to the views rather than the post itself and is extremely low effort.

cases.policyUnderTest: A truthful holder statement is allowed and the explanation is graded normally.

task.targetText: Hyphae commits each epoch's complete score set to Solana as a Merkle root. Contributors receive non-transferable points first, then treasury rewards settle from the epoch allocation.

contribution.text: I hold MYCEL, and the delayed settlement makes sense to me because the epoch can be audited as one complete set before the treasury splits.

expectedPolicy.treatment: Natural, on-topic, and compliant. Grade the product reasoning normally; first-person ownership is not a buy or hold instruction. The reply earns solid credit but adds only a modest angle beyond the target.

founderLabels.reason: It follows the rules, stays on topic, and feels natural. It does not add much beyond the post, but it is a good contribution and the holder disclosure is allowed.

cases.policyUnderTest: Holder status is allowed but does not create quality by itself.

task.targetText: Hyphae commits each epoch's complete score set to Solana as a Merkle root. Contributors receive non-transferable points first, then treasury rewards settle from the epoch allocation.

expectedPolicy.treatment: Zero-quality contribution. The truthful holder statement is allowed, but it adds nothing to a target that is not asking about holders and must not be rewarded.

founderLabels.reason: It adds nothing, and the target is not about holders. The statement is permitted but should not receive a reward.

cases.policyUnderTest: Grounded and uncertain price or valuation speculation is allowed.

task.targetText: This epoch generated 12 SOL in protocol fees, up from 6 SOL last epoch. The eligible contribution pool grew 20%, while MYCEL supply stayed unchanged.

contribution.text: If fee growth holds while supply stays flat, a higher MYCEL valuation could make sense. Two epochs still isn't enough to call it a trend though.

expectedPolicy.treatment: Strong natural and organic engagement with real reasoning. The stated basis, uncertainty, and counterpoint prevent a price-policy breach. The voice may feel holder-like, but it does not prove ownership.

founderLabels.reason: Natural, organic engagement with thought and reasoning. It feels like the perspective of a holder while remaining uncertain and grounded.

cases.policyUnderTest: A hedge does not ground an unsupported target.

task.targetText: This epoch generated 12 SOL in protocol fees, up from 6 SOL last epoch. The eligible contribution pool grew 20%, while MYCEL supply stayed unchanged.

expectedPolicy.treatment: Low-effort unsupported price hype. 'NFA' adds a small amount of caution to the raw-quality judgment, but it does not replace an explanation connecting the target facts to the $1 prediction and does not remove the guideline breach.

founderLabels.reason: Low effort. The NFA disclaimer makes it somewhat better than the same unsupported target stated without any caution, but it still lacks reasoning.

cases.policyUnderTest: A factual premise does not excuse a buy instruction or guaranteed gains.

task.targetText: This epoch generated 12 SOL in protocol fees, up from 6 SOL last epoch. The eligible contribution pool grew 20%, while MYCEL supply stayed unchanged.

contribution.text: Fees doubled, so buy MYCEL now. Guaranteed 10x.

expectedPolicy.treatment: Maximum-severity hard zero. The direct buy instruction and guaranteed return each independently violate the rules and require a breach flag.

founderLabels.reason: Against the rules and must be flagged. Both the direct buy instruction and the guaranteed 10x claim are prohibited.

cases.policyUnderTest: An honest reward disclosure does not reduce writing quality.

task.targetText: Every scored contribution now has a public receipt with the rubric version, model, reasoning, prompt hash, and evidence hash. Admin corrections are appended instead of replacing the original score.

contribution.text: Disclosure: I can earn Hyphae points for this reply. The evidence hash still matters because changing the model output would change the receipt, so edits can't be hidden.

expectedPolicy.treatment: Almost-perfect reply-quality contribution. It clearly explains how the evidence hash works and sounds like someone who knows the project. Do not penalise the honest disclosure; X best practice and platform eligibility remain separate reviews.

founderLabels.reason: It explains how the mechanism works and is clearly written by someone who knows the project. The disclosure should not reduce writing quality, regardless of whether it is ideal for X distribution.

cases.policyUnderTest: A question already answered by the target does not add value merely because it is a question.

task.targetText: Epoch claims open Friday at 16:00 UTC and close Sunday at 16:00 UTC. Use /claim in the bot during that window.
task.brief: Ask a useful question or add an observation.

expectedPolicy.treatment: Very low effort because the answer is explicit in the supplied target. It does not break a rule, but question form alone creates almost no value.

founderLabels.reason: It is not against the rules, but it adds nothing because the answer is right there in the target.

cases.policyUnderTest: Naming the project does not establish context fit.

task.targetText: The public score page now shows the original model grade beside every admin correction.

contribution.text: I am really excited to see what AI trading agents will look like on MYCEL.

expectedPolicy.treatment: The writing is understandable enough for a 50 raw-quality target, but its relationship to the score-page announcement is unclear. The MYCEL name-drop does not create context fit, so the off-topic gate still makes credited quality zero.

founderLabels.reason: It is unclear how the reply relates to the target. The sentence can receive some raw writing credit, but it misses the announcement's subject.

cases.policyUnderTest: Polished contrast and rhetorical structure alone do not prove AI authorship.

task.targetText: A Hyphae receipt keeps the model output, rubric version, and any later admin correction in one public audit trail.

contribution.text: A score receipt is more than a number. Not just model output, but a trail anyone can inspect. Hyphae is showing that contribution rewards don't need a black box.

expectedPolicy.treatment: A normal, acceptable comment that confirms the post in different words. It is solid rather than exceptional, and one polished contrast should not trigger an AI-writing flag without stronger combined evidence.

founderLabels.reason: It confirms the post in a different way and resembles what a normal community comment would look like. It is okay, but it does not add enough for an exceptional score.

cases.policyUnderTest: Multiple concrete AI-writing signals should be reported structurally.

task.targetText: A Hyphae receipt keeps the model output, rubric version, and any later admin correction in one public audit trail.

contribution.text: This groundbreaking initiative serves as a testament to Hyphae's pivotal role in the evolving Web3 landscape, highlighting its commitment to transparency, innovation, and community empowerment.

expectedPolicy.treatment: Coherent enough for a 70 raw-quality target, but over-complimentary, promotional, and non-organic. Flag the combined templated signals by naming textual evidence rather than asserting hidden authorship.

founderLabels.reason: It feels AI-based, is too over-complimentary, and does not look organic, even though the prose is coherent.

cases.policyUnderTest: A single common AI-associated word does not prove an unedited AI draft.

task.targetText: A Hyphae receipt keeps the model output, rubric version, and any later admin correction in one public audit trail.

contribution.text: This transparency is crucial for contributors because they can match each score to the receipt and see every later correction.

expectedPolicy.treatment: A normal organic reply that says what is expected from the target. Grade it normally; the word 'crucial' alone is insufficient for an AI-writing flag.

founderLabels.reason: It sounds organic and says what would reasonably be expected in response to the post.

cases.policyUnderTest: The scorer must not invent image content or hard-zero a plausible image-specific reply when only extracted text is supplied.

task.targetText: A new way to inspect every score. pic.x.com/hyphae-demo

contribution.text: Putting the model score and admin correction side by side makes the audit trail much easier to follow.

expectedPolicy.treatment: An acceptable 75-quality reply if the image shows the referenced layout. Do not invent what the image contains or apply an off-topic hard zero solely because extracted text cannot verify the detail; state the evidence limitation. Product direction is to include images in scoring because they carry important context.

founderLabels.reason: This would be an acceptable reply if the image shows the side-by-side layout. Images need to be included in scoring because they often communicate a large part of the post.

cases.policyUnderTest: A code-only submission is spam rather than a contribution.

task.targetText: The next epoch starts Monday. Read the published rubric before submitting a contribution.

expectedPolicy.treatment: Zero-quality code-only spam with no interpretable relationship to the target. Do not infer copying or coordination beyond the supplied text.

founderLabels.reason: The code is not interpretable in context and appears to be spam.
